scene.note: The page was only ever checked on a laptop. After this issue the same files lay it out well on Tomasz's phone and on a wide screen.

steps.note: On Tomasz's phone the menu sits on top of the library name, and the two parts of each card footer run into each other.
Both rows, the page header and each card's .event-footer, are held together with floats in styles.css. Take every float out.
Make each row a flex row at every width, with its two groups at opposite ends.
When the phone is too narrow for both groups, the second one moves to a new line instead of landing on the first.
Without being told, a phone draws the page as if it were a wide screen and shrinks it. The head of index.html tells it the page is as wide as the device.
Every card is a fixed share of the row, so on the phone there are still three thin strips side by side.
Make .event-list a grid that decides how wide the cards are, and take away the widths the list items and the cards set for themselves.
On a wide screen the grid holds at least two cards side by side.
On the phone the cards stack in a single column, one under the other.
With the cards narrower, the pictures stick out past the card's edge on Tomasz's phone.
Let each picture in an .event card shrink with its card, so a narrow card holds the whole picture.
The reading challenge card has a hashtag with no space in it, so it runs off the edge of the card.
Tell the browser it may break a word that would overflow, and the hashtag folds onto the next line inside the card.
